items.title: [Bug] StackOverflowError during clean config generation in 26.3.4
items.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

26.3

### Mod version

26.3.4 [release]

### Modloader version

Fabric 0.19.5

### Modpack info

Nope

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [x] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

https://p.kdan.dev/7lgHrL9

### Issue description

Description:
Upgrading from 26.3.3-beta with pre-existing configuration files loads normally without issues. However, when starting Jade 26.3.4 with a clean profile or after deleting the Jade configuration folder, the game immediately crashes during startup with java.lang.StackOverflowError. This issue is consistently reproducible in a minimal environment with only Jade 26.3.4 and Fabric API installed.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Install Jade 26.3.4 on Fabric mc26.3.
2. Delete the 'config/jade' folder or any jade*.json config files.
3. Launch the game.
4. The game crashes during plugin initialization.

Root Cause Analysis:
During fresh configuration creation, WailaConfig.fixData() calls ClientPluginConfig.ensureEntry(), which fires notifyChange(). The CorePlugin change listener then immediately invokes IWailaConfig.get() before initialization is finalized, causing JsonConfig$CachedSupplier to re-invoke WailaConfig.fixData() in an infinite re-entrant recursive loop.


Minecraft crashed without a crash report. The logs have been uploaded to `paste.kostromdan.dev`:
### [latest.log](<https://p.kdan.dev/7lgHrL9>)   |   [crash_assistant_app.log](<https://p.kdan.dev/sDDso4M>)   |   [modlist.txt](<https://p.kdan.dev/KwdbSVI>)
